newsitem.title: KENYA: Eritrea says Zaire force lacks clear mandate.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea says Zaire force lacks clear mandate.

text.p: Eritrea said on Monday a multinational force being assembled for eastern Zaire lacked a clear mandate and ignored recommendations of regional leaders.
Under these circumstances, the Eritrean foreign ministry said Eritrea would withhold a pledge it made last week to contribute a contingent to the multinational force.

"The government of Eritrea wishes to express its serious misgivings on the multinational force of intervention on eastern Zaire that is apparently underway," the foreign ministry said in the statement faxed to Reuters in the Kenyan capital Nairobi.

"The contemplated intervention force does not, in fact, have a clear mission or mandate; completely ignores the core recommendation of the Nairobi summit and the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) central organ resolution that calls for the separation of intimidators and bonafide refugees," it said.
It said the force had not identified where, how and to whom humanitarian assistance would be provided, did not know with whom to coordinate and had not determined its duration.

It said the Nairobi summit in early November unequivocally defined objectives of such a force as creating a temporary sanctuary to facilitate voluntary repatriation of bona fide refugees by separating them from armed militia.

"The intervention now underway contravenes these salient points...It will not only induce a vicious circle and perpetuate the circumstances which bred the present crisis but is also fraught with new and dangerous consequences," it said.
On Thursday, Kenya chided the United Nations for failing to discuss the intervention force with African nations.

President Daniel arap Moi told a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit that his country was "surprised to learn through the media, and without consultation with us, that there is to be international intervention in the region."

"The Nairobi (November 5) summit passed resolutions which among others called for the respect of the territorial integrity of Zaire and a plea for humanitarian support for the victims of this conflict," Moi said in his speech to the summit.
He said the resolutions passed were clear and the United Nations Security Council had endorsed them.

"My colleagues and I expected the United Nations to consult with us through the secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) before embarking on any action directed at the solution of the crisis," Moi added.
